stem.text: An open-top baking pan is made from a square sheet of tin 48 inches on a side by cutting a square of side x from each corner and folding up the sides. The baking pan can be at most 4 inches tall. Find the largest possible volume of the baking pan, in cubic inches.

worked_solution.text: The baking pan has height x and a square base of side \( 48 - 2 x \), so its volume is \( V(x) = x\left(48 - 2 x\right)^{2} \).
The cut must be positive, less than half the sheet, and at most 4, so the domain is \( 0 < x \le 4 \).
\( V'(x) = 12 \left(x - 24\right) \left(x - 8\right) \), which is zero at \( x = 8 \) and \( x = 24 \); only \( x = 8 \) lies strictly inside the sheet.
The critical point \( x = 8 \) is beyond the height limit, and \( V'(x) > 0 \) for every x in \( 0 < x \le 4 \), so V is increasing there and is largest at the right endpoint \( x = 4 \).
The largest volume is \( V(4) = 4\left(40\right)^{2} = 6400 \) cubic inches.

options.derivation: the side of the base at the optimum reported instead of the volume
the height limit left out of the domain, so the critical point x = 8 is used
the side of the cut square, where the maximum occurs, reported instead of the volume
